weather_line: Fog settling in the hollows · a stranger is coming · recovery rope already coiled

stories.headline: A Voice From the Gorge: Someone Claims to Have Been to Harlan's Hollow, and Has Opinions About the Creek Crossing
body: A source has emerged. He is described by those who know him as 'a man who has been places' and by those who have hiked with him as 'technically correct, usually.' His name has not been confirmed for publication. He approached Steve at the feed-supply counter in Jellico on Tuesday morning and said, without preamble, that Harlan's Hollow is passable in dry conditions, that the third creek crossing is not as wide as it looks but is considerably deeper, and that the northern approach from the ridge access road Christine has already mapped is, in his view, the only sensible one. He used the word 'sensible' twice. Steve wrote nothing down. He did not need to.

The source departed before Steve could ask how he knew about the Hollow, how he knew about the access road, or how he knew they were going. The feed-supply counter attendant reported that the man had been standing there when she arrived this morning and had not, to her knowledge, purchased anything. A single duck was found on the Jeep's mirror when Steve returned to the car park. It was not there when he went in.

stories.headline: Tuesday Reaches the Bank in Good Order; Christine Has Already Spoken to Three Accounts It Did Not Know Were Complicated
body: Tuesday's business proceeded without incident, which is to say it proceeded exactly as Christine had anticipated and in the sequence she had prepared for. Three accounts flagged by the overnight goblin review as 'requiring senior attention Monday' were resolved before Tuesday had finished clearing the lobby floo. The accounts in question have been reclassified as 'resolved, precedent-setting.' The goblins have not disputed this.

Griphook the Younger, when informed that the three accounts were settled, said only that the paperwork was filed correctly and the margins were adequate. This is, sources confirm, the highest praise he has given any paperwork in fourteen months. He has not been told that Christine deliberately left one margin slightly wider than standard. She will tell him when it becomes useful.

stories.headline: A Winch Appears on the Workbench; Steve Says It Is 'Just in Case'; the Jeep Has Already Accepted This as Fact
body: The table now holds the ordnance chart, the trail guide, the recovery rope, Christine's access-road notes (two pages, annotated, with a creek-depth estimate she will revise upward by morning), and, as of Tuesday afternoon, a hand-winch retrieved from the third shelf of the garage at four-seventeen. Steve set it on the workbench first and looked at it for a moment, then moved it to the table without explanation. He said 'just in case' once, to no one in particular.

The Jeep, when Steve started it briefly at half past four — 'checking something,' he said — ran for three minutes and forty seconds before he switched it off. The engine note, several household observers noted, sounded satisfied. The creek crossing, the unnamed source had said, is deeper than it looks. The winch fits in the rear cargo space with the recovery rope and still leaves room for the trail flasks. Christine measured this at four forty-one and did not say anything about it, which means she is pleased.

stories.headline: Ministry Issues Tuesday Bulletin Confirming Tuesday; Notes the Emergence of 'an Unregistered Hollow-Adjacent Source'; Adds Him to a List; the List Already Has the Hollow on It
body: The Ministry of Magic's Tuesday bulletin, released at the customary time and in the customary format, confirmed that Tuesday had arrived and was proceeding within standard weekly parameters. It further noted, under Item Nine (Supplementary Observations, Unclassified), that a source of unknown origin had provided expedition intelligence to a civilian party operating in the Appalachian Highlands region and that this source had subsequently departed 'without filing the required Form 7-C (Unsolicited Terrain Advisory, Non-Ministry Personnel).' The Ministry has added the source to its list. The source is, the bulletin observes, also not registered. The Hollow, also not registered, is on the same list, one line above. The duck has not been logged. The Ministry is aware of the duck.

familiars_corner: Lucy: Was observed near the garage workbench at four-fourteen, three minutes before the winch was retrieved. She has offered no comment and her expression suggests she does not intend to.

Ellie: Discovered the winch on the table this evening, sniffed it carefully for forty seconds, and then looked at the recovery rope as though seeing it for the first time, despite having slept next to it for two days. She appears to have reached a conclusion, though no one is certain what it was.

Jersey: Has determined that the trail guide, open to the creek-crossing page, makes an acceptable chin rest. He has been in this position for one hour and eleven minutes. The page is warm. He considers this an improvement over its previous, un-rested state.
founding_editor_note: A winch is only 'just in case' until it isn't — I put one in every build, and I was right every time. The bracket holding the garage shelf it came off, incidentally, I would have set half an inch lower. — D.

in_brief.sport: Regional Creek-Depth Estimation Championship: Christine leads the field with a revised estimate that she has not yet announced but which is already more accurate than anyone else's.
in_brief.forecast: Fog through Wednesday; clearing on the ridge by Thursday; the creek will be exactly as deep as Christine thinks it is.

storyline_updates.title: The Second Circle
storyline_updates.summary: Day 3: A source has appeared — a man at the Jellico feed-supply counter who knew about the Hollow, the creek crossing, and the access road without being told. He left a duck on the Jeep's mirror and departed without purchasing anything. The table now holds chart, trail guide, recovery rope, Christine's annotated access-road notes (creek depth revised upward), and a hand-winch Steve retrieved from the garage. The Jeep has been started and sounds satisfied. The Ministry has logged the source and the duck; neither is registered. Day 4 should move toward departure readiness: the final items assembled, a departure window confirmed or narrowed to a specific morning, and possibly one more word from the mysterious source — or from his duck.
